#1380. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

In a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

The work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

#1379. Napoli sign agreement to purchase land for new state-of-the-art training centre

Napoli President Aurelio De Laurentiis has confirmed that he has signed a preliminary agreement to purchase up to 18 hectares of land to build a new state-of-the-art training centre in the Qualiano area of Naples, with work scheduled to get underway in early 2027.

De Laurentiis took to social media on Wednesday afternoon to share images of the signing of the contracts, along with the message: “It’s done, full steam ahead.”

According to Sky Sport Italia, Napoli have agreed to purchase 13 hectares of land in Qualiano with an option for an additional five hectares.

The new Napoli training ground project will include eight pitches, plus two more if they acquire the additional five hectares, a specialist goalkeeping facility, a small stadium for youth team matches, reception and lounge areas for players and staff, office spaces and a pond that will provide water for pitch irrigation.

The works are expected to get underway in early 2027. There are still a few bureaucratic steps to undertake first, though, including gaining formal permission to build upon the plot, which is currently designated as agricultural land.

“Napoli has always had its home in Castel Volturno, where we won two league titles,” De Laurentiis told reporters on Wednesday.

“Have you seen where Maradona trained? Today is definitely a new beginning, because we have completed the first phase and now we can move onto the second.”

#1378. Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'

#1377. Maguire Axed as Rashford Decision Made - Pochettino's First Man Utd XI v Liverpool Predicted

Mauricio Pochettino will lead Manchester United out for the first time on Sunday afternoon when they take on arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

The Red Devils opted to make a change in the dugout during the international break, with Michael Carrick sacked after just one win in the opening ten games of the season, leaving the team 18th in the table, just one point off the bottom.

Pochettino has been appointed on a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, giving him time to revolutionise Man Utd, and has now officially taken over his duties after helping the USMNT to an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the Nations League during his final two games as their boss.

United now face arguably their toughest game of the season in his first outing, and the Argentine will have just three days of training with his new squad of players to try and prepare them for the clash.

So what will his first starting lineup look like, based on the players he is expected to have available? GIVEMESPORT has had a go at predicting it...

The goalkeeper position is one that is not up for debate at this stage, and Senne Lammens will be the starting goalkeeper for now. The defence, however, is not as clear-cut.

£111m duo Luke Shaw and Harry Maguire are listed as doubts after recent injury issues, and the likelihood of Pochettino taking risks immediately is slim to none. That means Patrick Dorgu should get the nod at left-back, having got a goal and assist as a substitute in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa before the international break.

In central defence, Leny Yoro has been impressive this season and should start in his preferred centre-back role. At the same time, Lisandro Martinez is available again after his suspension and Pochettino is likely to lean on his fellow countryman to provide some experience and leadership. At the same time, Diogo Dalot should shift back over to his preferred right-back position.

Mauricio Pochettino's pending arrival at Man Utd could be about to save one star's Old Trafford career.

The midfield underwent a major rebuild in the summer, and despite the team's struggles this season, the midfield has been far from the biggest issues at the club.

Kobbie Mainoo has continued to prove himself as a leader on the pitch and will retain his place in the heart of the midfield, but with Carlos Baleba injured, Pochettino will have a decision to make over who partners him.

£50m summer signing Andrey Santos is the more defensive-minded option, but Youri Tielemans has the experience and quality on the ball to provide what Pochettino likes, and the Belgian is more likely to get the nod in this game as a result.

In the number ten role, Bruno Fernandes has started to rediscover some form after scoring against Roma and Aston Villa, while he also found the net for Portugal in their 3-2 win over Wales this week, and so the skipper will keep his place in the team as a key player.

Man Utd have found their goalscoring boots again in recent games, and Pochettino will be keen to maintain that momentum in this game.

Benjamin Sesko remains sidelined until the new year with a shin problem, and while Joshua Zirkzee netted in the draw with Aston Villa he is likely to continue on the bench with Bryan Mbeumo getting the nod as the starting striker, much like how Heung-Min Son did at Spurs at times under Pochettino. Amad Diallo's work rate and dribbling is likely to be something the new boss likes, and should keep him in on the right wing ahead of Shea Lacey for this game.

On the left, Marcus Rashford is expected to be a key player under the Argentine, who is understood to be 'obsessed' with the Carrington graduate. But the England international has missed the last month with hip and groin problems, and he is unlikely to be rushed back, meaning Matheus Cunha will get a chance to stake his claim for a starting spot at Anfield.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Liverpool: Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Martinez, Dorgu; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

A tense summer looms at United as contract dilemmas, injury comebacks and looming sales promise to reshuffle the defensive spine.

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Pochettino will begin his new role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending new job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

#1374. Erling Haaland Was Spotted Playing GTA V Before Champions League Final

Footballers are often big fans of video games. From Grand Theft Auto to FIFA/EA Sports FC, many big names over the years have been known to be avid gamers.

Current Ballon d'Or holder Harry Kane spoke about how playing Fortnite helped him when he was away with England at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, recalling: “As silly as it sounds, playing Fortnite passes the time quite well. There are quite a few of us playing a few games of that.”

Fellow England star Cole Palmer recently got suspended for streaming the new FC27 on Twitch ahead of its agreed embargo time. There are many more footballers who love gaming, and Erling Haaland can be counted among them.

Haaland has hit 36.5 km/h — but how does that compare to Mbappe, Ronaldo, Messi, an NFL sprinter and Usain Bolt himself?

The Manchester City and Norway star is among the best players on the planet right now, and has been for some time. Scoring goal after goal for club and country, there are few more fearsome strikers in the game.

Still only 26, the Man City ace has already won two Premier League titles, two FA Cups, the League Cup and the Champions League with his current team. Undoubtedly, his best season came in 2022/23, when he won the treble under Pep Guardiola.

Across that campaign, the Norwegian scored 52 goals in 53 games for City (finishing second in the Ballon d'Or race). The crowning moment, however, came on 10 June 2023. The English side would beat Inter Milan 1-0 to win the Champions League for the first time in the club's history and seal that aforementioned treble.

It was perhaps the biggest achievement of Haaland's career to date, and yet on the eve of the final, he appeared to be in an incredibly relaxed mood. Indeed, the striker was actually spotted playing GTA V on PlayStation 5.

The final that year was held at the Ataturk Olympic Stadium in Istanbul, Turkey, so Haaland wasn't playing it at home. This may explain why he appeared to be playing the Prologue mission, having clearly just started a new save on the GTA V story mode.

The Man City ace was soon asked to switch games and play FIFA 23 (the franchise's final release under EA Sports), but hilariously shot back:

"I’m in the middle of a heist! I need the cash, so… The police is after me!"

Haaland is evidently a big fan of GTA, having also been once heard whistling the game's soundtrack at the Etihad after beating Napoli in the Champions League

With all that in mind, the Man City star will surely be one of many desperate to play the new Grand Theft Auto VI when it is finally released on Thursday, 19 November. He's actually on the record as saying: "I can’t wait for the new GTA.”

He's not the only star footballer to play video games shortly before a career-defining match. Most notably, Italy's Andrea Pirlo played PlayStation all day before then going on to win that 2006 World Cup final that evening.

Famously, he recounted in his autobiography:

"I don’t feel pressure... I don’t give a toss about it. I spent the afternoon of Sunday, July 9, 2006 in Berlin sleeping and playing the PlayStation. In the evening, I went out and won the World Cup.”

No wonder the iconic midfielder is regarded as one of the coolest footballers to ever grace the sport.

#1372. David James Names Best Atmosphere He Ever Played In - Not Anfield or Wembley

David James had a fruitful career playing for Liverpool, Aston Villa and England, among others, in some brilliant stadium atmospheres.

Wembley Stadium is the national stadium, but the Premier League also has incredible stadiums such as Liverpool's Anfield, Manchester United's Old Trafford, Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, Man City's Etihad Stadium, Chelsea's Stamford Bridge, Newcastle's St James' Park, and Aston Villa's Villa Park as part of it, where players are either backed to the hilt by home fans, or face a hostile welcome when appearing as an opponent.

English football is the home of some of the greatest stadiums in world football, and as a result, it often produces some of the best atmospheres too.

When playing at the highest level too, players will get to travel around the world and compete in continental competitions or at international level, meaning they get to play at other iconic venues and soak in the atmosphere there too.

One player who was able to do that during his 26-year career in professional football was former goalkeeper David James.

James represented top clubs such as Liverpool, Man City, Portsmouth, and Aston Villa during his career, while he also earned 53 caps for the senior England national team, appearing at Euro 2004, the 2006 World Cup, and 2010 World Cup.

The 6ft 5' star made a name for himself as a fine shot-stopper, and even had a brief stint playing as a striker under Stuart Pearce for 6 minutes in a Premier League game as they chased a victory. He is best remembered for his time as Liverpool number one, where he made 277 appearances between 1992 and 1999.

Having played at the top level, James played all over the world and in some of the greatest stadiums. He also played in some huge matches with great atmospheres, including four FA Cup finals, a League Cup final, and World Cup knockout stage games.

But while speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, on behalf of LiveFootballTickets, the 56-year-old revealed that while he loved playing regularly at Anfield and Wembley in his career, neither of those venues was the best atmosphere he ever played in.

“'Best' is a very subjective term," he said.

"Of course, winning at Anfield is special. I was actually thinking about playing games at Anfield, but my experience in India with Kerala Blasters stands out.

"The team had just been created for the Indian Super League. We played a game in Kochi, and it was the loudest football match I’ve ever played in. There were 60-odd thousand people making noise two hours before the game, all the way through it, and then even more after we won.

"It was incredible to understand how football had gripped a part of the nation that wasn’t renowned for football, and how much passion the supporters had.

"Anfield and Wembley are obviously massive stadiums and massive occasions, but the atmosphere at Wembley or Anfield is a frequent thing. What we had in Kochi was the first time for that team, and that was part of the reason why.

"I’ve said this to many people: experiencing that made me fall even more in love with football."

James spent one season playing professionally in India, having been signed by the club's owner and cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar as player-manager.

The team finished as runners-up in the league, before James retired and left the club at the end of his contract. He returned for a short stint as manager once again in 2018. But his time in Asia was clearly very special to him and left a lasting impression, as he still recalls his time there very fondly.

Ferguson visited the stadium 33 times in his legendary career.

Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

England, who romped to a 3-0 lead with a superb display before the hour mark, were forced to weather a late onslaught from the Spanish after Elliot Anderson was shown a red card in the 63rd minute of the Nations League clash.

#1370. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1369. Carnevali: ‘Juventus unable to make significant investments on players, it’s a challenge’

Juventus CEO Giovanni Carnevali has admitted that it is difficult for the club to invest heavily on new signings due to their UEFA settlement agreement and says that this is a result of mistakes that have been made in previous seasons: ‘I have plenty of confidence, but it takes time’.

Carnevali spoke to the media on Wednesday after an appearance at the RCS Sport Industry Talk in Milan.

Carnevali says that in order to achieve sporting results, clubs are required to invest heavily in their playing staff, but says that this is difficult for Juventus at the moment as a result of the settlement agreement they signed with UEFA back in July.

Juventus were found to have broken the football earnings rule, which allows a maximum aggregate deficit of €60m across a period of three financial years, which for Juventus, covered 2023, 2024 and 2025.

As a result, Juve were handed a conditional fine of up to €20m, at least €6m of which is guaranteed, and signed a three-year settlement agreement that requires them to meet strict financial targets set out by the European governing body. Full details of the settlement agreement are available on the UEFA website.

Carnevali discussed the complications that the settlement agreement has brought to Juventus on Wednesday.

“Today, our main difficulty relates to the settlement agreement,” said Carnevali (via Sky). “If we want to make significant investments on players, we find we are unable to do so. It’s a challenge because in order to achieve sporting results, you need to invest in great players.

“The club has carried out a capital injection, which means that we have made some mistakes in past years. I have plenty of confidence, but it takes time.”

Carnevali added: “Being at Juventus is a source of pride. It’s a forward-thinking club. If we’re talking about Juve, we’re talking about the stadium that we own, about JHotel, about JMedical. Over the years, Juventus has always tried to look ahead, thinking about opportunities that extend beyond football.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

So why don’t you try and bring players through the youth system instead of wasting what little money you do have on rubbish?

#1368. Pochettino Wants Man Utd Chiefs to Sign Balogun, He's Ready to Explode

Manchester United are ready to back new manager Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window.

Pochettino officially landed in Manchester on Wednesday to officially take charge of Man United, having managed the United States to a 2-0 win against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning, UK time.

Now, the Argentine will get to work to try and pick up a positive result when the Red Devils travel to Anfield to face Liverpool in the former Tottenham boss' first match in charge of the club.

United have made a terrible start to the Premier League season and lie in the relegation zone after 10 matches, winning just one of those at home to newly-promoted Ipswich Town.

They could actually be bottom of the table by the time they kick off on Merseyside, should Sunderland register at least a draw at Aston Villa and Crystal Palace beat Coventry City under new manager Thomas Frank.

Pochettino knows he must use his current squad to get out of trouble until the New Year, with the potential that Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Marcus Rashford could all be available at Anfield after various injury issues.

Beyond that, it appears as though INEOS are ready to back the 54-year-old in the market, as they consider strengthening three different positions.

According to GIVEMESPORT sources, United are looking at signing a new centre-back in January with Fulham's Calvin Bassey a player who is appreciated.

The Nigeria international is able to play in central defence and at left-back, another position the Red Devils want to strengthen, and GMS has also revealed that Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto is 'one to watch' ahead of January.

As well as the defence, United chiefs are also looking at bringing in a new striker for Pochettino, given they have navigated the majority of this season without Benjamin Sesko because of injury, which has seen the likes of Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and even Bruno Fernandes fill in as makeshift number nines.

United hold an interest in Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin, although GMS revealed that the centre-forward is set to sign a new contract to stay at Elland Road instead.

Meanwhile, Monaco's Folarin Balogun could be on the move in January with the Ligue 1 outfit needing funds, and there will be links with United given Pochettino knows him so well and got the best out of him in a United States shirt.

According to the Telegraph, the Argentine head coach is actually ready to push United to sign the 25-year-old in the New Year, according to US sources.

There would be some uncertainty over whether Balogun would be a hit at Old Trafford if he joined mid-season, but there won't be many better striker options on the market in January than the former Arsenal man.

What is clear from Balogun's career so far is that he has largely been prolific wherever he has been, from Arsenal youth sides to the United States national team.

The 25-year-old, who was labelled 'insane' by teammate Christian Pulisic, is fast and has shown he is capable of spectacular finishes, and he can give the Red Devils what they have been missing in recent months in the absence of Sesko.

His movement is good, and you'd hope he could thrive from the creativity of Fernandes and others, and he is also clinical.

The other big benefit of signing Balogun is that, because he knows Pochettino's methods and tactics so well, he shouldn't need much time to bed in at Old Trafford.

Pochettino clearly has confidence in him and that has boosted the striker's confidence in front of goal, and he would be ready to explode at the Theatre of Dreams if he did make the move in January.

With Monaco needing the money, it will be interesting to see how much the 25-year-old will cost in January, given he came close to completing a £40m move to Everton on deadline day in the summer.

From United's point of view, a loan with an option to buy would probably be their preferred deal, but Monaco would likely want an obligation to buy to agree to that structure of deal.

Now we must see if Pochettino and United chiefs agree on the direction they should go in when it comes to identifying their number one striker target.

#1367. 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place…

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career

'After the session we had a coffee and Pep said to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

So what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

He tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'

#1366. Conte admits he thinks will return to Juventus and names two times he could have

Antonio Conte says he believes that he will end up back at Juventus as head coach one day and has named two instances over the last few years when he could have returned as head coach of the Bianconeri: ‘I know that eventually the circle will be closed’.

Conte, in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, has spoken about his connection with Juventus and his willingness to return and ‘close the circle’ with the club where he spent over a decade as a player and won three Scudetti as a head coach.

As a head coach, Conte won three back-to-back league titles in Turin, the first in the club’s run of nine consecutive Scudetti in the 2010s, and Juventus is still the only club where Conte has lasted any longer than two years in charge during his managerial career.

“I think that sooner or later the circle will close,” Conte confessed in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, which was teased on Wednesday.

“I know I left something behind and I know that eventually the circle will be closed with Juventus.

“There have been moments in the past where we could have reunited, but it’s been difficult because two things have to align. I have to be available and Juventus have to be looking for a coach who isn’t currently employed.”

Conte went on to pinpoint the two moments where he could have returned as head coach of Juventus.

“There have been two instances. Once, when Juventus decided to hire Maurizio Sarri, I was available and later ended up at Inter.

“Then there was a second time when I was free, just as Giuntoli arrived. Giuntoli decided to go for Motta and I went to Napoli.”

Conte also revealed that he had been on the verge of becoming head coach of Juventus in 2009, two years before he was actually appointed. He says that he was in the building and prepared to sign with the Old Lady just before leaving Bari, but a disagreement over the use of Diego saw the deal collapse.

Conte explained: “After my time at Bari, there was a possibility of my going to Juventus. I spoke several times with Castagnini and Secco, Ranieri was the head coach at the time, but eventually they let him go and brought in Ciro [Ferrara] for the final three matches, hoping to qualify for the Champions League.

“They knew perfectly well that I would have played a 4-2-4 formation, given that I would have had forwards like Mauri, Iaquinta, Trezeguet and Del Piero. I told them ‘look, as far as forwards go, we’re all set, we need to sign some wingers’. But for whatever reason, they ended up signing Diego from Werder Bremen instead, and then they called me.

“I remember that it was around the time of the Champions League final between Manchester United and Barcelona in Rome. They called me and said ‘look, we need you to come in because we still need some reassurances from you’. I was still at Bari at the time.

“Anyway, I went, walking in as the Juve manager and then we started talking. They asked me how I wanted to play, and I replied ‘with a 4-2-4’. They said ‘right, but where would you play Diego?’. I answered ‘look, you were the ones who signed him, even though I said that we already have four forwards. So I would play him alongside one of the strikers’.

“Then they told me ‘well, Diego wants to play in a 4-3-1-2’. Imagine my madness at the time. Although, that madness shows that I’m a very direct person who doesn’t make compromises. Anyone else, literally anyone else, would have said ‘sure, I’ll even play him in goal if you want, just let me sign the contract and I’ll join Juve’.

“I was moving from Bari to Juventus after all. But once they said that to me, I stood firm in my ideas, firm in my convictions, and firm in the fact that I wasn’t going to make any compromises or promise anything I knew I wouldn’t deliver.

“So, I told them ‘if a player decides how we play, then I’m not the right coach for you’. And that was it. I walked away and by the time I left that meeting, I was no longer the coach of Juventus.”

#1365. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1363. England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

#1362. Where Italy stand in FIFA World Rankings after latest international fixtures

Italy will end the calendar year in 14th place in the FIFA World Rankings following a 3-1 victory at home against France and a 4-1 defeat away against Belgium in the Nations League during the November international break.

Italy began the November international break rated as the 15th best national team in the world.

The 3-1 victory at home against France temporarily saw the Azzurri rise up to 13th, but the latest update to the FIFA Men’s World Rankings, which arrived on Thursday, sees them drop back down to 14th following the completion of the latest round of international fixtures.

There have been no changes to the top four-ranked national teams since the start of the November international break: World Cup winners Spain remain top of the rankings despite their recent defeat against England, World Cup finalists Argentina remain in second, France are still in third despite their defeat against Italy and England remain in fourth.

Morocco have risen two places in the rankings up to fifth, Portugal have dropped down one place to sixth, Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil have also dropped one place down to seventh, Belgium remain in eighth place, the Netherlands remain in ninth and Colombia have risen one place to complete the top 10.

Currently ahead of Italy in the rankings are Germany in 11th (up two places), Switzerland in 12th and Mexico in 13th (down three places).

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Immediately after the Win against France, Italy rose to 12th Rank (+3) and not 13th. After the Loss against Belgium, Italy dropped by two Ranks.

#1361. How Vinicius Jr's lavish summer holiday has left him playing catch up: Real Madrid star admits he 'trained less' while on luxury yacht trip and blames Brazil's early World Cup exit - and 'overwhelming' Arsenal rumours - for sluggish start to the season

Published: 09:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:48 EST, 16 November 2026

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger says he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal  and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr)

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr)

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and said that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr)

'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

He has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January

The winger is currently serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

#1360. Romelu Lukaku announces 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026

Romelu Lukaku has announced his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

'16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

[The performance] was a little bit mixed. It’s a tough enough place to come and the start we had put us in a difficult situation. I thought we grew into the game, had four big chances and [score one or more] and the game looks really different. They were really good chances.

And then the red card which I thought was a really poor one. It’s difficult after that. Disappointed that with the chances we had we didn’t [get] more [out of the game].

I haven’t seen [Martinez’s interview]. After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be a little bit emotional. I have not seen it so I don’t think it is the right time for me to comment on it.

I fully know we all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through. We have a big game on Sunday.

[How do you sum up the performance?] Really poor, Really poor. I have to control myself a lot. Sometimes it’s a mirror of the reflection of how our club is.
